Select the bandwidth of a geographically weighted regression

Source: R/gwr-bandwidth.R
ef_gwr_bandwidth.Rd

Selects a fixed (metres) or adaptive (k nearest stations) bandwidth by minimising AICc or the leave-one-out cross-validation score over a recorded search, and returns the full profile of the criterion (dev/specs/gwr-forcing.md section 4).

AICc (decision GW-02): $$AICc = 2n\ln\hat\sigma + n\ln(2\pi) + n\,\frac{n + tr(S)}{n - 2 - tr(S)}, \qquad \hat\sigma = \sqrt{RSS/n},$$ with n the number of stations of the fit and tr(S) the trace of the hat matrix; defined only when \(n - 2 - tr(S) > 0\). Leave-one-out cross-validation: $$CV = \sum_i (y_i - \hat y_{\ne i})^2,$$ where \(\hat y_{\ne i}\) is the local fit at station i with its own weight set to zero (the bandwidth \(b_i\) is computed with the station included), obtained exactly as \(e_i / (1 - s_{ii})\).

Usage

ef_gwr_bandwidth(
  y,
  x,
  coords,
  kernel,
  adaptive = FALSE,
  criterion,
  search,
  scale_covariates = TRUE,
  station_id = NULL
)

Arguments

y

Numeric vector: the response at each station, in the unit of the variable (e.g. degC for air temperature).

x

Numeric matrix (or data frame of numeric columns) with one row per station and one column per covariate, with unique column names (e.g. elevation [m]). The intercept is added internally.

coords

Numeric matrix with two columns: projected coordinates (x, y) of the stations [m]. Distances are Euclidean in this CRS (decision GW-09); geographic coordinates (degrees) must be projected first.

kernel

Character, no default (decision GW-04 is open): one of "gaussian", "exponential", "bisquare", "tricube", "boxcar".

adaptive

Logical. FALSE for a fixed bandwidth in metres, TRUE for an adaptive bandwidth given as k nearest stations (the k-th smallest distance, counting the regression point itself when it is a station). Taken from bandwidth when that is an earthflux_gwr_bandwidth object and adaptive is not supplied.

criterion

Character, no default (decision GW-05 is open): "AICc" or "CV".

search

The settings returned by ef_gwr_search().

scale_covariates

Logical. Whether to centre and scale the covariates internally (by their mean and standard deviation over the stations of the fit) to condition the local systems. Coefficients are always reported in original units and predictions do not change.

station_id

NULL or a vector of unique station identifiers. By default names(y), rownames(x) or the row numbers.

Value

An object of class c("earthflux_gwr_bandwidth", "list") with elements value (b [m] or k), type ("fixed" or "adaptive"), unit ("m" or "neighbours"), kernel, criterion, criterion_value, global (criterion, AICc and CV of the global OLS model, the b = Inf reference), profile (data frame with one row per evaluation: bandwidth, criterion, feasible, reason of infeasibility, aicc, cv, enp = tr(S), rss, min_nonzero (smallest number of neighbours over the stations) and stage: "grid", "refine" or "global"), search (effective bounds and settings, number of evaluations, tie rule), stations (station_id, status, exclusion_reason), flags and provenance. Pass it to ef_gwr_fit() as bandwidth.

Details

A bandwidth is infeasible when, at some station, the local design is rank deficient ("rank_deficient") or has fewer than min_neighbours neighbours ("few_neighbours"), when AICc is undefined ("aicc_undefined": n - 2 - tr(S) <= 0, where the formula would give spuriously low values) or when a LOO residual is undefined ("loo_undefined": s_ii = 1). Infeasible bandwidths are kept in the profile and never selected. Ties of the criterion are resolved by the smallest bandwidth. The search is deterministic.

Flags (object scope): EF_GWR_BW_AT_BOUND (the best grid value is at a search bound; it is returned, not extrapolated), EF_GWR_BW_MULTIMODAL (more than one local minimum among the feasible grid values), EF_GWR_AICC_UNDEFINED (criterion AICc undefined in part of the interval) and EF_GWR_GLOBAL_PREFERRED (the global OLS model has a criterion not larger than the selected bandwidth; the finite optimum is still returned). Excluded stations: EF_GWR_STATION_EXCLUDED (record).

Errors: earthflux_gwr_insufficient_stations (n < p + 3), earthflux_gwr_no_feasible_bandwidth (field profile), earthflux_missing_input (a search setting needed and not given), earthflux_unknown_method (kernel or criterion).

AICc conventions and other implementations

Three different quantities are called "AICc" for the same fit by GWR software (dev/specs/gwr-forcing.md section 4.2). EarthFlux uses n = number of stations of the fit, \(\hat\sigma\) the maximum likelihood estimate sqrt(RSS/n) and tr(S) (aicc_definition = "gollini2015_tr_S_sigma_ml"). This is exactly GW.diagnostic$AICc of GWmodel 2.4-1, checked in the tests. GWmodel reports as enp the quantity 2 tr(S) - tr(S'S) (EarthFlux enp_alt), although its AICc uses tr(S). Algebraically, with K = tr(S) + 1, the penalty n (n + tr S)/(n - 2 - tr S) equals n + 2K + 2K(K + 1)/(n - K - 1): a Gaussian AIC with K parameters plus a small-sample correction.

Verification status

AICc form: VERIFICADA as content of Gollini et al. (2015; preprint arXiv:1306.0413v2, section 6.1, p. 20), who attribute it to Hurvich and Simonoff (Hurvich, Simonoff & Tsai, 1998; not read); sigma is not specified there. As an EarthFlux definition: CANDIDATA (corroborada), reproduced by GWmodel. LOOCV: CANDIDATA (corroborada). The search (log grid plus Brent refinement; exhaustive search over k) is a design choice; its settings have no default (GW-05).

References

Gollini, I., Lu, B., Charlton, M., Brunsdon, C., & Harris, P. (2015). GWmodel: An R package for exploring spatial heterogeneity using geographically weighted models. Journal of Statistical Software, 63(17). doi:10.18637/jss.v063.i17

Hurvich, C. M., Simonoff, J. S., & Tsai, C.-L. (1998). Smoothing parameter selection in nonparametric regression using an improved Akaike information criterion. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 60(2), 271-293. doi:10.1111/1467-9868.00125

Examples

coords <- cbind(c(0, 10000, 0, 10000, 20000, 30000, 25000, 5000),
                c(0, 0, 10000, 10000, 0, 30000, 15000, 25000))
elev <- cbind(elevation = c(100, 300, 500, 200, 800, 1200, 650, 900))
ta <- c(20.0, 18.9, 17.5, 19.6, 15.4, 13.1, 16.2, 14.6)
bw <- ef_gwr_bandwidth(ta, elev, coords, kernel = "gaussian",
                       criterion = "AICc",
                       search = ef_gwr_search(n_grid = 20, tol = 10,
                                              upper_factor = 2))
bw
#> <earthflux_gwr_bandwidth>
#> Kernel: gaussian; fixed bandwidth = 84852.814 m
#> Criterion: AICc = 7.0474135 (global OLS: 6.8436811)
#> Search: [25495.098, 84852.814] m, 20 grid values, tol = 10 m; 21 evaluations
#> Minimum neighbours: 3 (mathematical_minimum); feasible evaluations: 20 of 21
#> Flags (warning): EF_GWR_BW_AT_BOUND [1/1]
#> Flags (info): EF_GWR_GLOBAL_PREFERRED [1/1]
fit <- ef_gwr_fit(ta, elev, coords, bandwidth = bw)
